# init:service

Bootstraps a complete microservice project from scratch.

## Usage

```sh
mkdir my-service && cd my-service
waffle init:service
```

The command prompts for the service name, then generates the full project layout.

## Generated files

### Entry point

**`cmd/app/main.go`**

The binary entry point. Calls `config.Init()` which resolves the DI container and wires the closer:

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "mymodule/config"
)

func main() {
    application, err := config.Init()
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("failed to start: %s\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    application.RunUntilStop()
}
```

### Configuration wrapper

**`config/config.go`**

A thin wrapper that delegates to the diogen package:

```go
package config

import (
    "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/app"
    "mymodule/config/diogen"
)

func Init() (app.App, error) {
    return diogen.InitDi()
}
```

### DI registrations

**`config/di/di.go`**

The single file where all DI wiring lives. Contains the `//go:generate` directive and an `InitDi()` function. Add tool registrations and your own types here. The `app.App` wiring must always be present:

```go
//go:generate go tool diogen -output config/diogen/di_gen.go -pkg diogen $GOFILE

package di

import (
    "gitlab.com/gorib/di"
    "gitlab.com/gorib/env"
    "gitlab.com/gorib/pry"
    "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/app"
)

func InitDi() {
    di.Wire[pry.Logger](func() (pry.Logger, error) {
        return pry.New(env.Value("LOGLEVEL", "info"))
    })

    // Add tool and domain registrations here

    di.Wire[app.App](app.Init, di.Args(map[string]any{
        "commands": di.Tags[app.Command](app.CommandTag),
    }))
}
```

Each tool page shows the exact block to copy inside `InitDi()`. Example for the HTTP tool:

```go
di.Wire[app.BaseCommand](
    func() app.BaseCommand { return app.NewCommand("http", "Start web server") },
    di.For[whttp.HttpCommand](),
)
di.Wire[whttp.MiddlewareList](whttp.NewMiddlewareList, di.Args(map[string]any{
    "middlewares": di.Tags[whttp.Middleware](whttp.MiddlewareTag),
}))
di.Wire[whttp.HttpCommand](whttp.NewHttpCommand, di.Tag(app.CommandTag))
```

### Diogen adapter

**`config/diogen/di.go`**

Hand-written adapter between the generated container and the application. Calls `InitApp()` (generated), wires the closer, and returns `app.App`:

```go
package diogen

import "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/app"

func InitDi() (app.App, error) {
    di, err := InitApp()
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    application := di.AppApp()
    if closable, ok := application.(app.HasCloser); ok {
        closable.SetCloser(di.Shutdown())
    }
    return application, nil
}
```

**`config/diogen/di_gen.go`**

Generated DI container. **Do not edit.** Regenerated by `make generate` every time you change DI registrations in `config/di/di.go`.

### API initialization

**`api/<service>/init.go`**

Empty initialization file for the service API package. Add HTTP route registration and gRPC handler registration here.

**`api/<service>/proto/.gitignore`**

Ensures the `proto/` directory is tracked by git even when empty.

### Project files

**`.env`**

Local environment variable overrides for development. Loaded automatically by `gitlab.com/gorib/env` on startup. Not committed to git.

**`.gitignore`**

Standard Go gitignore plus `.env`.

**`Makefile`**

Standard targets:

| Target | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `make generate` | Run all code generators (DI, store) |
| `make .tidy` | `go mod tidy` |
| `make build` | Build the binary |
| `make run` | `go run ./cmd/app` |

## Post-generation steps

After writing all files, `init:service` runs:

```sh
go get gitlab.com/gorib/digen
make .tidy generate
```

This installs the DI code generator and produces the initial `diogen/di_gen.go` so the project compiles immediately.

## What to do next

1. Add your environment variables to `.env`
2. Call tool initializers in `config/di/di.go`
3. Run `waffle make:domain <name>` to create your first domain
4. Run `make generate` after each DI change
